summary.text: 会 is the simplified form of 會, used for assembling, meeting, and a meeting. Its visible 人+云 shape comes from later cursive writing; it is not evidence that the character was originally built from “person” and “cloud.”

formation.text: The current graph is a later simplified graphic form of 會, whose early construction is interpreted in competing ways. One paleographic account reads early forms as 合 combined with a vessel-like element, possibly showing parts that fit together; Xu Shen’s earlier lexicographic analysis instead gives 亼 and an abbreviated 曾. The exact object and original sense are not settled. The modern 人+云 appearance does not establish a historical compound of those elements.

components.text: In 会, 人 is the visible upper element, but it is not supported as an ancient semantic or pictorial component. The character’s 人+云 appearance belongs to its later cursive-derived form.
In 会, 云 is the visible lower element. No evidence here establishes it as an ancient phonetic or semantic component; its appearance results from the later graphic form of 會.

history.text: 会 is documented as a cursive-derived variant of 會, later used widely in regular writing and adopted as the PRC simplified form. Its modern parts therefore should not be projected back as an ancient 人+云 construction. No historical glyph images were available for direct inspection in this dossier.

Early forms of 會 have been analyzed as 合 with a vessel-like element, while Xu Shen described the graph as 亼 with an abbreviated 曾. The proposed vessel-and-lid reading is itself disputed in detail; the central shape and depicted object are not established by the inspected evidence.

uncertainties.text: The fragmentary oracle-bone phrase 會我 is only a possible early use meaning “meet.” Separate reported bronze and Warring States examples use 會 for meeting or joining, but they do not establish whether “fit together,” a vessel or lid sense, or “meet” came first, nor prove a semantic path between them.

The dossier gives no evidence for a sound component in 会 or for 云 as a phonetic element in this graph. The historical phonological records concern readings of 會 itself and do not supply a component-to-character sound comparison for the visible 云.

senses.period: Warring States and later securely reported; earlier oracle-bone use tentative
senses.text: Bronze and Warring States examples are reported for meeting at a place, joining ideas, and meeting in alliance. A fragmentary oracle-bone example may have this sense, but that reading is explicitly tentative.
The character is used as a noun for a meeting or gathering. Japanese え also has a dated use for a gathering, including a religious assembly, in an early ninth-century text.
会 also denotes an organization or association. The dossier does not establish when this noun sense developed from the sense “meeting” or “gathering.”

senses.period: historical; chronology relative to meeting unresolved
senses.text: Historical dictionary citations attest 會 as a noun for a lid or cover. This lexical sense is compatible with some proposed vessel interpretations of the graph but does not establish that interpretation or its priority.

developments.text: Using the verb meaning “meet” for the noun “meeting” is a plausible relationship, but the supplied attestations do not document the transition or its chronology.

limitations.text: The earliest secure dating of the “meet/assemble” sense relative to the lid or cover sense is unresolved in this dossier. The proposed connection from fitting a lid to joining or meeting remains an interpretation, not a demonstrated sequence.

overview.text: 会 is the simplified form of 會 and means to meet, gather, or a meeting. Its visible 人+云 shape reflects later cursive writing, not an original “person + cloud” construction.

components.text: Visible in the later form, but not established as an ancient component meaning “person.”
Visible in the later form, but not established as an ancient sound cue for 会.

relationships.text: 人 is visible in the later cursive-derived simplified graph, but the evidence does not support a historical semantic, pictorial, or phonetic role for it in 会.
云 is visible in the later cursive-derived simplified graph, but the evidence does not support a historical semantic or phonetic role for it in 会.
会 arose as a cursive-derived graphic form of 會 and was adopted as its simplified form.
